headline: Anthropic estimates that robots could do about a third of physical work tasks but are cost-effective today for only about 300,000 US jobs.
score_reason: Relevant labour-market analysis, but it is a company-authored estimate, read only through a trade outlet's summary.
importance_line: Taxi drivers and warehouse packers are most exposed in the near term, though the 2.8 million figure assumes robot costs fall 20 percent, which the analysis says could take seven years.
summary: Facilities Dive reports on an Anthropic analysis estimating that robots can already do around a third of physical work tasks but are cost-effective for only about 300,000 US jobs today, rising to 2.8 million if robot costs fall 20 percent, which the analysis says could take about seven years. Taxi drivers and warehouse packers are the most exposed, while work needing fine dexterity or interpersonal skill is least at risk.
notes: Anthropic is the author of the analysis; this is a company estimate, not an independent finding.
